tasks.title: Capture the trace pair on your usual route
tasks.criteria: Two captures, same route: base-game.html?trace=1, then base-game.html?trace=1&tracephases=0. Both saved to the performance log.
tasks.why: Gives the six encode stages as capture-wide percentiles, the instrumentation's own cost, the granted device limits, and names any shader compile.
tasks.outcome: Read. Device grants 8 vertex-stage storage buffers, so the pulled forest is admitted. The overhead pair was inconclusive: the three timers-off runs (p50 57, 57, 32 ms) varied more than the timers-on runs differ from them.

tasks.title: Look at drones, vehicles and grass
tasks.criteria: Spawn a drone and a vehicle and fire an AGM: no missing part, wrong colour, or see-through hull. Watch grass wind, walk across a rebase, then repeat with ?grassScope=object: no frozen wind, wrong rate, or grass jump in either run.
tasks.why: These are the two shipped changes whose failure would be visible: shared craft materials and the render-group grass uniforms.
tasks.outcome: Ticked with no note, so I am reading it as: nothing looked wrong. If anything did, reopen it with a note.

tasks.title: Run the refresh audit on the route
tasks.criteria: base-game.html?refreshaudit=1 on the same route, then save a capture.
tasks.why: It never skips; it reports where a skip of the refresh would have been wrong on the spawn building, structures and roads, and what its own check costs.
tasks.outcome: Read, about 33,000 frames. Zero wrong skips, but nearly every declared object changed every frame because its model-view matrix depends on the moving camera, and the check cost 0.4 to 0.6 ms per object. The skip extension is marked not worth building in this form.

tasks.title: Forest: default against 'One merged draw, compact'
tasks.criteria: Tree look panel, LOD2 branch submission. Switch to 'One merged draw, compact' after tasks 1 to 3. Far trees still there and same shape as before. If they vanish or go black, note it and switch back.
tasks.why: The pulled forest has compiled headless only; this is its first device compile and first render. The fallback should already have switched back on a validation error and the capture says why.
tasks.notes: the 2 logs before the lod2 and 1 off are just lod2 off. the stationary lod2 and 1 off is actually lod 012 off. then i kept those off and turned off terrain. then i turned off grass too. i was able to get 65-75 fps, but movement still dips. therse were on base-game.html?refreshaudit=1
tasks.outcome: Your note describes the LOD rung toggles: all rungs off took the standing frame from about 24 to 16 ms. That is what removing the vegetation saves (geometry, shading, shadows and culling as well as the objects), an upper bound on any forest change, not a per-object figure. Every capture has the submission select at variants, so the compact mode itself has not been rendered yet. Reassigned as task 6.

tasks.title: Decide on pushing the branch
tasks.criteria: Say push, or not. About 36 commits since 492de74 are local; the friend test runs off 492de74.
tasks.why: Task 2 came back clean, so the visible risks left are the forest modes, which are off by default.

tasks.title: Render the compact forest mode and compare it to the default
tasks.criteria: Tree look panel, 'LOD2 branch submission', with all three LOD rungs ON and trees on. Stand in one spot facing a tree line. Capture once at 'One draw per variant', then switch to 'One merged draw, compact' (the forest rebuilds), same spot, capture again. Note whether the far branches look identical, and whether anything vanished or went black. If the console shows a forest fallback warning, note its message.
tasks.why: The device admits the mode, but it has only ever compiled headless. This is its first render. Same spot, same content, the two captures are the only fair test of what merging one role saves or costs; do not have ?trace=1 or ?refreshaudit=1 on for these.

tasks.title: Walking A/B: one terrain worker against two, on the minimal scene
tasks.criteria: Trees off (all LOD rungs off) and grass off, as in your 14:50 runs. Walk the same route twice, about 30 s each: base-game.html?terrainworkers=1, then base-game.html (default, 2 workers). One capture each.
tasks.why: With trees and grass off the frame sits at 15 to 17 ms standing but still dips walking, and the dip frames carry busy terrain workers and gaps between frames. One worker against two on the same route tests what the setting does to those dips. It does not say why a frame was late; that needs a DevTools trace.

tasks.title: GPU timestamps on while walking
tasks.criteria: Same minimal scene and route as task 7, default workers: base-game.html?gputime=1, walk about 30 s, one capture. Note if the page says the device does not support timestamps.
tasks.why: The dip frames show 20 to 30 ms of gap between frames with no long task on the main thread. If GPU time rises in those frames the GPU is involved; if not, it is not. Either way this does not by itself attribute the gap. Timestamp frames are not comparable with untimed ones, so this is its own capture, with no trace or audit flag.
